transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Cyclone Finance), Sana Ahmed (Cyclone), Evan Brooks (Cyclone), Mira (note-taker)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown; discuss dedicated vs hosted for finance workloads and next steps for a pilot.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. we're gonna run through the Console today — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then a cost breakdown by route. feel free to interrupt.
[00:18] Raj Patel: Thanks Maya, excited — we want to see how we'd get visibility into token costs per feature.
[00:25] Diego Alvarez: cool, i'll share my screen. quick note, i'm gonna demo with a sample app that mirrors your payment-notification and fraud-check routes. some names might look like "fraudcheck_v2" or similar.
[00:45] Sana Ahmed: quick ask — can you call out where KMS keys and audit logs appear in the console? that's high priority.
[00:53] Maya Chen: yes, we'll show the security section but the main focus is usage + cost. Diego, over to you.

[01:05] Diego Alvarez: okay loading console... top-level view is the Usage Overview. you can see tokens consumed over time, cost by day, and spikes. (screen noise) so here we filter by model and by route. i'll switch to the per-route dashboard.
[01:32] Diego Alvarez: this is per-route breakdown. left pane has route list: payment-confirmation, fraud-check, customer-chat. the center is latency p95/p99, error-rate, and tokens-per-request. bottom shows cost attribution — both compute and model unit cost.
[01:50] Evan Brooks: is that cost just model price or does it include batching efficiency math?
[01:54] Diego Alvarez: good question. cost = model unit price * tokens + runtime overhead. we also surface batching efficiency as an adjustment — so you can see effective cost per 1k requests given autoscaling and batching settings. sometimes the transcription says "batching efficency" but the numbers are correct.

[02:20] Raj Patel: do you show cost per customer segment or per API key? we'd like to attribute to business units.
[02:27] Diego Alvarez: yes, you can tag routes and keys. the dashboard supports group-by for API key, team, or route. we'll show an example grouping by api_key and by tag.
[02:40] Diego Alvarez: also note the prefix/KV cache savings — when you have repeated prefixes the console estimates token savings and shows projected cost delta if cache hit-rate improves.
[02:58] Sana Ahmed: hmm, for us fraud-check has lots of repeated prompts, that could be big.

[03:05] Diego Alvarez: exactly. here's the cost waterfall for a selected route: raw model cost, caching savings, batching delta, infra overhead. we break down in USD and in tokens.
[03:20] Maya Chen: i'll point out per-route SLOs — you can set latency SLO targets and the console will show projected cost to meet the SLO vs lower-cost configuration. it helps customers understand the latency vs cost tradeoff.
[03:36] Raj Patel: can we see an example? show what happens if we tighten p95 by 50ms.
[03:40] Diego Alvarez: yep, toggling the slider here — projected cost goes up because more dedicated capacity or lower batch windows are used. those numbers are simulated from your historical distribution.

[04:05] Evan Brooks: what about model variants? like using a cheaper quantized variant for low-risk routes?
[04:10] Diego Alvarez: we surface model variants and automatic fallback policies. you can create routing rules: e.g., fraud-check -> try quantized-4bit first, fallback to fp16 if quality triggers. the console shows historical fallback rate and estimated cost/quality impact.
[04:28] Maya Chen: we often recommend a canary: run 10% of traffic on cheaper variant and watch quality metrics; the console will flag regressions compared to the baseline.

[04:45] Raj Patel: regarding dedicated vs hosted — we have compliance needs for card data. what's the recommended path?
[04:52] Maya Chen: for PII and strict compliance, Redwood Private or Dedicated is most common. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and VPC peering; Private gives customer-managed control plane. both support KMS/HSM and audit logs.
[05:07] Sana Ahmed: is KMS integrated with AWS KMS and GCP KMS? we use AWS KMS.
[05:12] Maya Chen: yes, we support AWS KMS and commonly used HSM providers. Diego will follow up with the integration doc.

[05:30] Diego Alvarez: circling back to cost — i'll open the cost-explorer. you can drill from account-level down to route and then to individual request types. here's a sample breakdown: payment-confirmation — 1.2M tokens last month -> $720 model cost, infra overhead $140, net $860. fraud-check — 3.6M tokens -> $1,900 model cost, but caching saved ~30% ($570 saved). these are example numbers; we'll run your real traffic to get exact.
[06:05] Raj Patel: do you show per-token unit price? we need to reconcile with our finance team.
[06:09] Diego Alvarez: yes each model has unit price shown; cost explorer includes negotiated rates and committed discounts if you have dedicated/reserved capacity.

[06:22] Evan Brooks: can we export these dashboards to CSV or reporting APIs?
[06:26] Diego Alvarez: exportable CSV and an API for cost queries. also scheduled reports to Slack or email.

[06:40] Raj Patel: think about retention — we need usage logs for 12 months for audit.
[06:47] Maya Chen: retention is configurable; enterprise plans can get longer retention and archived logs. Private deployment also keeps logs in-customer control.

[07:02] Sana Ahmed: any limitations around on-prem? we have some services that are air-gapped.
[07:08] Diego Alvarez: Private supports on-prem packages; we usually do a short design review. note that kernel optimizations and some monitoring features differ slightly on air-gapped installs but core cost analytics are available.

[07:30] Raj Patel: what about attribution for multiple teams using same model? we want chargeback per team.
[07:36] Diego Alvarez: use API keys + tags. Console allows cost allocation rules — you can define percentages or tag-based allocation. we also support automated invoice exports to your billing system.

[08:00] Evan Brooks: are the dashboards realtime? we need near real-time for ops.
[08:04] Diego Alvarez: near real-time — usually 1-2 minute lag for usage metrics; cost estimates can be slightly delayed while aggregation runs but routes/latency show up within minutes.

[08:20] Raj Patel: is there an example of the pilot scope? what do you need from us to run a benchmark?
[08:25] Maya Chen: typically sample traffic, target routes, success criteria (latency, cost per transaction), and test accounts/api keys. Diego, summarize the pilot steps.
[08:33] Diego Alvarez: sure — step 1: provide sample traffic and prompts; step 2: Redwood runs 2-week benchmark on hosted/dedicated variants, we collect per-route metrics; step 3: analyze cost and quality; step 4: recommend config and cost-saving levers (caching, batching, quantization).

[08:58] Raj Patel: timeline? we want a decision by end of June.
[09:02] Maya Chen: that's feasible. Pilot in early May, results mid-May, then procurement in June.

[09:12] Sana Ahmed: on procurement: what security docs can you share? SOC 2, ISO?
[09:16] Maya Chen: SOC 2, ISO docs, penetration test summary are available — we'll share via our secure portal. Diego will drop the link.

[09:28] Diego Alvarez: i'm posting the dashboard JSON and a runbook in the chat now. (link pasted) note: the dashboard JSON includes the per-route filters and cost calculations — you can import it to see identical views.

[09:48] Evan Brooks: great. quick note on quality: if we do quantized model for fraud-check, how do we measure false-positive regression?
[09:55] Diego Alvarez: we tie quality evals to a prompt set and run canary comparison. console surfaces regression alerts if metrics drift beyond thresholds.

[10:10] Raj Patel: any gotchas around tokenization differences across models?
[10:14] Diego Alvarez: yes tokenization differs; the console normalizes tokens to model-specific units and shows mapping. sometimes proper nouns or bin ascii cause token differences, so we recommend consistent model family for billing comparisons.

[10:32] Maya Chen: let's recap next steps. Maya sends pricing+pilot plan by Monday 2026-05-03. Diego will share dashboard JSON and KMS integration doc, Raj will send sample traffic by 2026-05-01. Schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-05-11.

[10:55] Raj Patel: sounds good. one last question — can we get a quick cost scenario: 5M tokens across two routes with 40% cache hit?
[11:02] Diego Alvarez: off the cuff: with our sample model rates that's roughly $2,600 model cost before cache; with 40% cache hits projected savings ~ $1,040, net $1,560 plus infra overhead. we'll run exact sims in the pilot.

[11:20] Evan Brooks: thanks all. do you have an onboarding checklist?
[11:24] Maya Chen: yes — Diego will attach the checklist; it covers tags, API key setup, network prep, and security docs.

[11:35] Mira: action items captured in notes.

[11:40] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and links.

[11:45] Raj Patel: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
